Pop Music of the 1950s in five graded experiences

Each experience is a short Ink and Toon animation built from your slides, followed by a check the student answers by tapping the objects in the scene. Every panel below is that beat’s key frame, rendered from the real scene code with the STAGE kit at 16 samples.

1

Small, cheap, and yours

Slides 5 and 211.9 s, 5 beats4 points

Answers the deck’s question: “What made 1950s teenagers a new kind of music audience?”

Beat 10.0–2.8 s

On screen78 RPMbefore 1949: big and heavyshattered if dropped!

Moves
Opens on a ten-inch 78 standing on its edge, rocking. It tips over backwards and breaks into seven pieces that skid outwards; impact ticks for two drawings.
Camera
Long lens, low, front-left of the record; slow drift in.
Sound
Shellac wobble ticks, a hard crack and scatter on the frame it breaks, then a beat of silence.

Beat 22.8–5.2 s

On screen45 RPM1949one song a side, under a dollar

Moves
A seven-inch 45 drops in beside the wreck, bounces twice and does not break. Three coins hop into a stack next to it.
Camera
Whips right in a third of a second to the 45, a little higher, then drifts.
Sound
Whoosh on the whip, two rubbery vinyl bounces, stamp on the word, three coin clinks.

Beat 35.2–7.4 s

On screenPOCKET RADIO1954a transistor radio fit in a pocket

Moves
A pocket transistor radio hops in from the right, lands with a squash and starts to play: notes pop out of the grille on twos.
Camera
Whips right to the radio, eye-level with it.
Sound
Plastic tock on landing, dial click, a tinny square-wave riff from the radio.

Beat 47.4–10.5 s

On screenTELEVISIONU.S. homes with a TV (about)1950 9% / 1955 65% / 1959 86%

Moves
A television set drops in. Its screen snaps through three readings: 1950 9%, 1955 65%, 1959 86%; the rabbit ears twitch on each.
Camera
Whips right and back to take in the whole set.
Sound
Heavy cabinet thud, CRT switch-on, a rising blip for each number, the last one a ding.

Beat 510.5–11.9 s

On screensmall, cheap, and yours

Moves
Nothing new arrives: the 45, the coins, the radio and the TV sit together as one teenage kit, radio still playing.
Camera
Pulls back to hold all three inventions; holds for the last second.
Sound
Paper slap for the caption, radio riff resolves, room tone.

Tap the three inventions that put music in teen hands.

Graded check4 points

After the animationTap the three inventions that put music in teen hands.

How
The table holds the broken 78, the 45, the pocket radio and the TV. Three taps; each right object pops and scores a point, the 78 buzzes. Then: "About how many U.S. homes had a TV by 1959?" 9% / 65% / 86%.
Camera
Holds on this framing; the scene is live 3D, so taps land on the objects themselves.
Sound
A ding and the object’s own sound for a right answer, a low buzz for a wrong one.
2

Two worlds

Slides 3 and 411.2 s, 4 beats6 points

Answers the deck’s question: “How was a crooner’s pop song different from rock and roll?”

Beat 10.0–2.6 s

On screenCROONERa soft, warm voice, close to the mic

Moves
Opens on the crooner’s microphone. Soft cream sound-waves and round notes drift out of it slowly, re-drawn every third drawing.
Camera
Long lens, level with the microphone, drifting right.
Sound
A warm sine hum of a held note with slow vibrato, brushed-snare hiss, room tone.

Beat 22.6–5.0 s

On screenCROONERbig orchestras, songs written by pros

Moves
Three pages of sheet music flutter down and land in a neat pile beside the microphone; the soft notes keep drifting.
Camera
Whips a little left and higher to make room for the pages.
Sound
Three paper landings, a soft string-pad chord under the hum.

Beat 35.0–8.0 s

On screenROCK AND ROLL1955loud beat, electric guitar

Moves
The camera whips to the other end of the table: a solid-body electric guitar hops in, its cable snaps into a small amplifier, and the amp jumps on every hit, throwing out bolts and jagged lines.
Camera
Fast whip right across the empty table, then a slow drift.
Sound
Whoosh, wood tock, jack click and hum, then a loud buzz-and-thud backbeat on each amp jump.

Beat 48.0–11.2 s

On screenTRADITIONAL POPparents and whole familiesROCK AND ROLLteenagers

Moves
Both ends of the table at once: the microphone still croons softly on the left, the amp still thumps on the right and three 45s pop into a pile beside it. Each side gets its audience caption.
Camera
Pulls back to a wide two-shot and holds.
Sound
Soft hum left, loud backbeat right (panned), three vinyl pops, two paper slaps for the captions.

Pop or rock? Tap the microphone or the guitar for each clue.

Graded check6 points

After the animationPop or rock? Tap the microphone or the guitar for each clue.

How
Six clue cards come up one at a time ("big orchestras", "loud beat", "teenagers", "Patti Page, Nat King Cole", "jukeboxes, 45s, DJ radio", "radio and TV variety shows"). Tap the microphone for traditional pop or the guitar for rock and roll: right answers make that side play, wrong ones buzz.
Camera
Holds on this framing; the scene is live 3D, so taps land on the objects themselves.
Sound
A ding and the object’s own sound for a right answer, a low buzz for a wrong one.
3

Three styles in one

Slide 612.9 s, 5 beats7 points

Answers the deck’s question: “Which three older styles blended to make rock and roll?”

Beat 10.0–2.2 s

On screenRHYTHM & BLUESa driving beat, shouting vocals, honking sax

Moves
Opens on a 45 player with a teal-label record tipped towards us above its fat spindle. It levels and drops onto the platter; the player squashes under it.
Camera
Long lens from the front-left, drifting.
Sound
Stamp for the word, a honked sax-like square note, vinyl slap and thud on the landing.

Beat 22.2–4.4 s

On screenCOUNTRYguitars, storytelling, and a twang

Moves
A mustard-label record pops in above the first, levels and drops on top of it.
Camera
Snaps round to the front.
Sound
Stamp, a twangy plucked note with a pitch bend, slap and thud.

Beat 34.4–6.6 s

On screenGOSPELpowerful singing and call and response

Moves
A cream-label record pops in, levels and drops: three records stacked on the spindle.
Camera
Snaps round to the front-right.
Sound
Stamp, a two-note call and answer on voices-like tones with a hand clap, slap and thud.

Beat 46.6–9.4 s

On screenROCK AND ROLLa new sound, about 1954

Moves
The tone arm swings over, the stack spins up with speed lines, squashes down and bursts into ONE record with a persimmon label.
Camera
Whips in closer and higher over the platter.
Sound
Motor whirr rising, a riser, then an impact and a bright guitar-like stab on the frame of the burst.

Beat 59.4–12.9 s

On screen1 2 3 4backbeat: clap on 2 and 4

Moves
The record plays. Four count badges light in turn, twice through: on 2 and 4 the badge jumps big, the player hops and clap marks fly; 1 and 3 stay small.
Camera
Eases back to show the counts over the player; holds.
Sound
Kick-like thud on 1 and 3, loud snare-clap on 2 and 4, walking bass tones; ends on the last clap ringing out.

Two tasks: pick the three styles that blended, then clap the backbeat.

Graded check7 points

After the animationTwo tasks: pick the three styles that blended, then clap the backbeat.

How
Five records lie in front of the player (rhythm and blues, country, gospel, crooner pop, doo-wop): tap the three that went on the spindle (3 points). Then the count runs 1-2-3-4 twice and you tap or press space on 2 and 4 (4 claps, scored on timing).
Camera
Holds on this framing; the scene is live 3D, so taps land on the objects themselves.
Sound
A ding and the object’s own sound for a right answer, a low buzz for a wrong one.

How teenagers heard the music

Slide 1014.9 s, 6 beats6 points

Answers the deck’s question: “Name three ways teenagers listened to music in the 1950s.”

Beat 10.0–2.2 s

On screenRECORD SHOP45 rpm single: one hit a side

Moves
Opens on a crate of 45s. A coin flips in and lands on the crate; one 45 jumps up out of it, bought.
Camera
Long lens on the crate, slow drift.
Sound
Coin ping and clink, cardboard rustle, vinyl pop as the record jumps.

Beat 22.2–4.4 s

On screenBEDROOMa small record player of your own

Moves
The same 45 flies along the table and drops onto the spindle of a small record player; the arm swings over and notes rise.
Camera
Whips right, following the record to the player.
Sound
Swish, vinyl slap on the platter, needle crackle, a few notes of a tune.

Beat 34.4–6.6 s

On screenDINERjukebox: drop in a coin, pick a song

Moves
A coin arcs into the slot of a jukebox. Its arch flashes, the record in the window turns and notes come out.
Camera
Whips right to the jukebox, pulled back for its height.
Sound
Coin in a metal slot, mechanical clunk, the same tune louder with a bass thump.

Beat 46.6–8.8 s

On screenANYWHEREtransistor radio: DJs played the hits

Moves
A pocket radio walks along the table by itself, bobbing on twos with speed lines behind it and notes trailing.
Camera
Whips right and tracks slowly with the radio.
Sound
Dial click, the tune thin and tinny (band-passed), plastic footsteps.

Beat 58.8–11.0 s

On screenLIVING ROOMtelevision showed the stars

Moves
A television set: its screen snaps on, a star pops onto it and twinkles, the rabbit ears twitch.
Camera
Whips right to the TV.
Sound
CRT switch-on thump and whine, applause-like noise burst, a ding for the star.

Beat 611.0–14.9 s

On screenSCHOOL GYMsock hop: dancing in socks, to recordsteens could choose, buy and carry their music

Moves
A record player spins a 45 on the gym floor and a pair of bobby socks dances beside it, hopping in turn. Holds on the dance.
Camera
Whips right to the last stop; eases back a little and holds the final second.
Sound
The tune at full strength with the backbeat, soft sock thuds on the floor, ends on a ding.

Four artists to remember

Slide 1113.5 s, 6 beats5 points

Answers the deck’s question: “Pick one artist. What did that person add to rock and roll?”

Beat 10.0–2.3 s

On screenSISTER ROSETTA THARPE1930sbefore them all: gospel on lead electric guitar

Moves
Opens on a hollow-body electric guitar standing alone. It rings: jagged lines and bolts jump off the strings on twos.
Camera
Long lens on the guitar, drifting.
Sound
A gritty electric guitar lick (sawtooth through a band-pass), hand claps, room tone.

Beat 22.3–4.5 s

On screenELVIS PRESLEYblended country and R&B: rock’s first superstar

A microphone. Two small 45s, a mustard one (country) and a teal one (R&B), fly in from either side, meet above it and burst into a gold star that stays, twinkling.
Camera
Whips right to the microphone.
Sound
Two swishes, an impact where they meet, sparkle and a ding for the star.

Beat 34.5–6.8 s

On screenCHUCK BERRYwitty songs about teen life; shaped rock guitar

Moves
A cutaway hollow-body guitar hops from side to side across the table (the duck walk) while a pencil scribbles lines onto a page beside it.
Camera
Whips right; drifts with the hopping guitar.
Sound
A two-string guitar riff, pencil strokes on paper, wood hops.

Beat 46.8–9.1 s

On screenLITTLE RICHARDgospel power, wild energy, pounding piano

Moves
An upright piano: keys slam down in changing clusters on every drawing pair, the whole piano shakes and impact ticks fly off the keyboard.
Camera
Whips right, a little wider for the piano.

Pounded piano clusters (stacked detuned tones) in fast eighths, a whoop-like rising tone.

Beat 59.1–11.3 s

On screenBUDDY HOLLYwrote his own hits, led his band The Crickets

A solid-body guitar hops in, a pair of horn-rimmed glasses lands in front of it, and a pencil writes on a page: his own song.
Camera
Whips right to the last artist.

Wood tock, a light click for the glasses, pencil strokes, a bright strummed chord.

On screenSister Rosetta TharpeElvis PresleyChuck BerryLittle RichardBuddy Holly

Pulls far back to hold the whole line-up for the last second and a half.

Who did it? Tap the artist’s set-up for each clue.

After the animationWho did it? Tap the artist’s set-up for each clue.

Five clues, one at a time in shuffled order ("wrote his own hits and led The Crickets", "pounding piano and wild energy", ...). Tap the matching set-up in the line-up: it plays its action if you are right. One point each.

What I assumed

  • ScopeI read “the facing slides” as what is on the slide faces, not the speaker notes, and “can be graded” as scored for a class. I built one experience for each of the five questions on the “Check your knowledge” slide, drawing on slides 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10 and 11. Slides 7 (doo-wop, rockabilly, teen idols), 8 (four records), 9 (inside the band), 12 (video list) and 13 (then and now) are not animated yet.
  • Scoring28 points in all, split as in the table above. The split, the tap-to-answer mechanics and the two decoy records in experience 3 (crooner pop and doo-wop, both from the deck) are my proposal, not from the slides.
  • WordingCaptions are shortened from the slide text to fit a caption box: “one song a side, under a dollar”, “a transistor radio fit in a pocket”, “big orchestras, songs written by pros”, “transistor radio: DJs played the hits”, “teens could choose, buy and carry their music”.
  • NumbersAll from the slides: 78s before 1949; the 45 in 1949; the pocket radio in 1954; U.S. homes with a TV about 9% (1950), 65% (1955), 86% (1959); rock and roll “about 1954” on slide 6 and “1955 and after” on slide 3 (I use each where its slide does); Sister Rosetta Tharpe “from the late 1930s”, shown as a “1930s” badge.
  • SizesThe slides say a 45 is seven inches wide. I drew the 78 at ten inches with a small centre hole and the 45 with its large centre hole; those proportions are general knowledge, not from the slide faces.
  • ObjectsThe deck shows objects, not portraits, and so do I. The pocket radio follows the 1954 Regency TR-1 in the slide photo (no aerial, round dial). The TV is a generic 1950s console set, not the Philco in the photo. Tharpe’s guitar is a generic hollow-body; Chuck Berry’s is a cutaway hollow-body like the Gibson pictured; Buddy Holly’s is a Stratocaster type. His horn-rimmed glasses are my addition and are not on the slide.
  • SymbolsA gold star stands for “rock’s first superstar”; a mustard record and a teal record stand for country and R&B, matching experience 3; a pair of dancing socks stands for the sock hop. The backbeat demo runs at 150 beats a minute, my choice.
  • BuildFinal piece: one self-contained HTML file with five chapters, each with play/pause, scrub, time, sound toggle and loop, then its check and a score card at the end (name, mark per question, total out of 28). Plus one MP4 per chapter. Panels here are block-outs: secondary motion, sound and the checks come after your OK.

Three things to decide

  1. Is five the right set?I can add experiences for slide 7 (three more sounds), slide 8 (four records), slide 9 (inside the band) or slide 13 (then and now), or drop any of these.
  2. How do you want to collect the grade?My default is a score card at the end showing the student’s name, each mark and the total out of 28, to show you or screenshot. If you would rather see a whole class’s results in one place, say so and I will build that in.
  3. Any beat, caption or object to change?Name the experience and beat number. On your OK I build the full animations, sound and checks exactly as boarded here.
